subject: Human Evolution
title: Scavenging Before Hunting
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Scavenging Before Hunting.

hook.text: A lion finishes eating and walks away. The carcass still has marrow-packed bones. Someone sneaks in.

buildup.text: Early hominins lacked weapons for big kills. But stone tools could crack bones that teeth couldn't.

discovery.text: Bone marrow is pure fat—the richest calorie source on the savanna, locked inside bones only tools open.

twist.text: Scavenging is risky: hyenas and vultures compete fiercely. Speed and group coordination mattered hugely.

climax.text: For hundreds of thousands of years, scavenging—not hunting—was probably the main route to meat.

punchline.text: We ate what others caught first.

quiz.question: Why was scavenging important for early hominins?
options: It gave access to high-calorie marrow without hunting skills
They were too slow to move
